entries.title: Quotes lists your own highlights too
entries.body: In your own articles, the Quotes panel now includes the passages you have highlighted, marked 'yours' and kept in the colour you gave them; press one to open its comments. They appear even before the AI has picked any quotes. Each quote's card also says who chose the words, you or the AI, and when, where a date was recorded; for older AI quotes it gives an 'on or before' date.

entries.title: Highlight or comment by selecting with a finger
entries.body: On a touch screen, selecting words in one of your own articles now shows a 'Highlight or comment' button beneath them, which opens the same comment box a mouse selection does. Before, a finger selection did nothing. Also on touch screens, the on-screen keyboard is put away when you send a message or run a search, and the buttons beside each paragraph sit further apart.

entries.title: Marginalia shows dates and where the argument turns
entries.body: Marginalia, the notes in the margin beside the article, now shows Timeline events beside the passages that date them, with dates given with their year. In your own articles it can also mark how a paragraph relates to the one before: 'so', 'but' or 'vs'. Turn it on with the Experimental features switch on your profile page.

entries.title: Quick search catches passing mentions
entries.body: Quick search now looks for passages that mention or discuss what you asked for, so it finds more passing mentions and may return more that miss the point. Its hits are marked beside the paragraph, not tinted. The 'flesh out' button is now 'thorough' and replaces the quick search; each saved search shows its colour.

entries.title: Tutorial keeps to the author's argument
entries.body: Tutorial, in Remember, now spends most of its questions on understanding and remembering what the author argued, and asks for your own view less often. It also welcomes you if you have not read or finished the piece. Where it can, pressing a citation in a reply briefly highlights the quoted words inside the paragraph.

entries.title: Tidier controls in the quiz and on cards
entries.body: In the Remember quiz, Answer is now a send icon, the answer box grows with what you type, and Next is emphasised once your answer is marked. The card on a glossary term puts its buttons on one row, with 'Open glossary' leading to the panel. The card on the strip showing where you are no longer repeats a heading.

entries.title: Library search links highlight accented words
entries.body: A passage search from your library now opens the article with the word highlighted as the article spells it, so 'café' is found where before nothing was highlighted. The contents list on an article's details page highlights the right section at larger text sizes. Copy link on the sharing card now says when copying failed.

entries.title: Referee keeps answers safe across tabs
entries.body: In Referee, running Claims in two tabs could let the older run overwrite the newer one, and a criterion still being answered could be deleted; neither can happen now. Its check for hidden instructions missed invisible characters on some pages; it now reads them. Referee sits behind the Experimental features switch on your profile page.
